grammar.title: Modal deduksi masa lalu
grammar.explanation: Untuk menyimpulkan apa yang terjadi di masa lalu, pakai modal + have + V3: 'must have' (hampir pasti), 'might/may have' (mungkin), 'can't have' (hampir pasti tidak). Setelah modal, selalu 'have', bukan 'had'.
examples: They must have misunderstood the deadline.
He can't have seen the email; he was on leave.
The file might have been deleted by mistake.

common_mistake.wrong: She must had forgotten the meeting.
common_mistake.right: She must have forgotten the meeting.

grammar.title: Nominalisasi untuk register formal
grammar.explanation: Laporan formal sering mengubah kata kerja menjadi kata benda (implement → implementation, decide → decision, reduce → reduction). Hasilnya lebih padat, objektif, dan tidak berfokus pada orang. Hindari kontraksi dan bahasa lisan dalam register ini.
examples: The implementation of the policy was delayed.
There has been a significant reduction in costs.
Our recommendation is the adoption of a shared calendar.

common_mistake.wrong: We decided to do it, but it got delayed because people didn't agree.
common_mistake.right: The implementation was delayed owing to a lack of consensus.

reading.title: Low-context and high-context communication
reading.text: The anthropologist Edward T. Hall distinguished between low-context and high-context cultures. In low-context cultures, such as the Netherlands or the United States, good communication is expected to be explicit: people say what they mean, and responsibility for understanding lies mainly with the speaker. In high-context cultures, including Japan and Indonesia, much of the meaning is carried by tone, relationships and what is left unsaid, so listeners are expected to read between the lines. Neither style is superior, but problems arise when they meet. A Dutch manager may interpret an Indonesian colleague's 'maybe' as genuine uncertainty, whereas it might have been a polite refusal. Conversely, direct feedback that sounds efficient in Amsterdam can come across as aggressive in Jakarta. Research on global teams suggests that the most effective leaders do not simply adopt one style. Instead, they articulate the norms explicitly at the start of a project, agreeing, for instance, that silence does not mean agreement and that disagreement in meetings is welcome.

options: It could actually be a polite 'no'

writing.prompt: Tulis laporan formal singkat untuk direktur dengan judul 'Improving the effectiveness of cross-border team meetings'. Pakai bagian Introduction, Findings, Recommendations, dan Conclusion. Gunakan register formal dan nominalisasi.
checklist: Ada judul bagian (Introduction, Findings, Recommendations, Conclusion)
Minimal satu modal deduksi (must have / may have)
Rekomendasi konkret dan bisa langsung diterapkan
useful_phrases: The purpose of this report is to ...
In light of these findings, the following measures are recommended:
writing.model_answer:
Report: Improving the effectiveness of cross-border team meetings

Introduction
The purpose of this report is to assess the effectiveness of weekly meetings between our teams in Jakarta, Singapore and Amsterdam, and to recommend improvements. The findings are based on a survey of 34 team members and a review of the minutes from the past eight weeks.

Findings
Firstly, meetings frequently overrun. On average, scheduled one-hour meetings lasted 78 minutes, mainly because discussions became sidetracked by issues relevant to only two or three participants. Secondly, participation is uneven. Colleagues in Amsterdam accounted for over half of all contributions, whereas several Jakarta-based engineers reported that they rarely felt comfortable disagreeing in a group setting. Thirdly, decisions are not consistently followed through. In five of the eight meetings reviewed, agreed actions had no named owner, and at least two important decisions must have been misunderstood, since they were later implemented differently in different offices.

Recommendations
In light of these findings, the following measures are recommended:
1. The circulation of a written agenda at least 24 hours in advance, with a time limit for each item.
2. The rotation of the facilitator role between offices, so that each region leads the discussion in turn.
3. The introduction of a short anonymous poll for key decisions, allowing quieter members to express disagreement.
4. The distribution of written minutes within two hours of each meeting, listing every action, its owner and its deadline.

Conclusion
The current meeting format does not make full use of the expertise available across the three offices. The implementation of the measures above would require minimal cost, yet it is likely to result in shorter meetings, broader participation and greater consistency in the execution of decisions. A review after one quarter is advised.

speaking.focus: Bentuk lemah 'must have' /ˈmʌstəv/, intonasi tegas tapi sopan pada 'I take your point', dan jeda pendek di titik koma.

speaking.prompt: Kamu fasilitator rapat. Dua rekan berdebat panjang tentang topik yang tidak ada di agenda, dan waktu tinggal 10 menit. Apa yang kamu katakan untuk mengembalikan rapat ke jalurnya secara diplomatis? (5 sampai 6 kalimat)
speaking.sample_answer: Sorry to interrupt, but I'm conscious that we've only got about ten minutes left. This is clearly an important discussion, and I don't want to cut it short unfairly. Could I suggest that we park it for now and set up a separate call with the two of you and anyone else who's directly involved? I'll note both positions in the minutes so nothing gets lost. In the meantime, let's go back to the release plan, because we need to reach a decision on that today. Does that work for everyone?

n1.them: Frankly, I think the Jakarta team's estimates are unrealistic. We've missed two deadlines already.
hints: tanggapi tenang dan netral: I hear your concern ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I hear your concern, Mark. Let's look at what actually caused the delays before we draw conclusions."

n2.them: The cause is obvious. They say yes to everything and then don't deliver.
hints: modal deduksi: There might have been ...

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "There might have been a misunderstanding. In some cultures, 'yes' can mean 'I heard you' rather than 'I agree'."

n3.them: That's an interesting point. So what would you suggest?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I'd propose the introduction of a written estimate review, where each team can raise risks before we commit."

n4.them: Fine, but who will make sure this actually happens? We've had good ideas before.

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "I'll own it. I'll send a draft process by Friday, and we'll review it at next week's meeting."

n5.them: Okay. I appreciate you taking this seriously. Anything else before we close?

fallback.feedback: Contoh: "Just to recap: we'll trial the estimate review for one month. Before we close, does anyone from Jakarta want to add anything?"

end.them: Good meeting, everyone. Thanks for steering that so calmly.
